problem:
Find the limit at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}6x+1\, & \text{ for }\,x\le \frac{1}{2} \\ -4{log}_{2}⁡x\, & \text{ for }\,x>\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide
examples.problem:
Find the left- and right-sided limits at $x=1$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by

$$
{\begin{aligned}6{e}^{x-1}\, & \text{ for }\,x<1 \\ {x}^{2}+2x+3\, & \text{ for }\,x>1.\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Approaching from the left, we have $x<1,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = 6e^{x-1}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}6{e}^{x-1} \\  & =6{e}^{1-1} \\  & =6{e}^{0} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Approaching from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = x^2+2x+3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}{x}^{2}+2x+3 \\  & ={1}^{2}+2(1)+3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
